steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (a field name is an interface others call), so I'm stopping before editing.

What I found:

- `routes/users.js:6` emits `userId` in the `GET /users` response. The rename is a one-word edit there.
- `README.md:3-5` says `GET /users` is consumed by the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export — and that "Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint."

So renaming in place is a breaking change for three consumers, one of which (shipped iOS builds) can't be updated in lockstep, and it contradicts the repo's stated versioning policy. The consistency goal is real — `listOrders` already uses `user_id` — but the in-place rename is the one option the README rules out.

questions.question: Renaming userId to user_id in /users breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export, and the README says field-name changes go through a versioned endpoint. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Add user_id alongside userId in the /users response. Non-breaking; new consumers can move to user_id while existing ones keep working. Leaves a deprecation to remove later.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: keep /users as-is and add a v2 response shape using user_id. Most work, but matches the documented contract process.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Change userId to user_id in routes/users.js only, as originally asked. Breaks the three documented consumers immediately, including already-shipped iOS builds.
